checklistTitle: Start with the record your decision needs

checks.title: Identify the site or asset
checks.detail: Use the correct parcel, building, facility, or utility connection. Record the boundary or ID you are making a decision about.

checks.title: Check the date and scope
checks.detail: Read the source, effective date, and fields that matter. Keep planned, approved, and operating assets distinct.

checks.title: Test it on real work
checks.detail: Use a guide’s named case or downloadable sample, then repeat the check on a site or portfolio you know.

guides.label: Find the parcel number for an address
guides.detail: Verify the assessor identifier, mapped lot, and jurisdiction before looking up related property records.

guides.label: Match the correct parcel and property unit
guides.detail: Check tax lots, parcel boundaries, condominiums, and ownership records before you join datasets.

guides.label: Get deed and ownership change alerts by address
guides.detail: Follow two NYC deeds through recording dates, instrument types and tax lot matches.

guides.label: Trace who owns a commercial property
guides.detail: Follow a deed, an entity filing, and the property link without assuming a shared name proves common ownership.

guides.label: Match building footprints to parcels
guides.detail: Compare mapped structures and their identifiers before aggregating a site or underwriting a portfolio.

guides.label: Check zoning districts and commercial overlays by address
guides.detail: Use three Brooklyn lots to see where the overlay covers the mapped address, the whole parcel, or only part of it.

guides.label: Check hospital, school, and fire service coverage
guides.detail: Compare travel times, grade-specific attendance maps, and emergency service boundaries for a proposed housing development.

guides.label: Compare housing vacancy and rent burden by census tract
guides.detail: Match tract boundaries across Census releases and test whether changes in vacancy and rent burden exceed sampling uncertainty.

guides.label: Find a certificate of occupancy by address
guides.detail: Check the city’s issued document, the correct building ID, and whether the certificate covers the space under review.

guides.label: Find and verify building permits
guides.detail: Check permit status, work scope, and the issuing agency record at the property level.

guides.label: Track permit changes by address
guides.detail: Compare new authorizations, expirations and completions against the source’s update dates. Keep one event for permits linked to several lots.

guides.label: Look up building energy use by address
guides.detail: Compare annual energy, reporting property IDs, meter scope and floor area before estimating operating costs or screening a retrofit.

guides.label: Check open building violations and correction records
guides.detail: Use the original building ID to verify summons status, balance and proof of correction on separate records.

guides.label: Screen land for wetlands and hydric soils
guides.detail: Compare mapped wetlands, soil map units and a Corps decision on a real property before drawing the development footprint.

guides.label: Review geologic maps, well logs, and site borings
guides.detail: Follow one industrial tax lot from its regional map to the nearby well reports and five on-site borings.

guides.label: Calculate slope and check usable acreage from lidar
guides.detail: Compare grid resolutions on the same land boundary and check the largest adjoining area that meets the slope cutoff.

guides.label: Check crop rotation, soil productivity, and irrigation
guides.detail: Compare annual crop maps against real plot records and confirm which source can support a farmland decision.

guides.label: Calculate soil productivity by parcel or field
guides.detail: Replay the USDA soil overlay at Iowa State’s Marsden Farm and compare acreage-weighted NCCPI with Iowa CSR2.

guides.label: Compare commercial property sales and lease terms
guides.detail: At one Manhattan tower, separate a deed from a lease assignment and compare recorded annual rent with a signed fixed-rent schedule.

guides.label: Check commercial space availability and lease rollover
guides.detail: Read dated leasing and occupancy metrics, verify available suites, and rebuild a public lease-expiration schedule.

guides.label: Size land for a data center
guides.detail: Use the facility load, utility pad dimensions, and largest connected buildable area to test a campus layout.

guides.label: Find industrial land for sale by acreage and zoning
guides.detail: Replay Virginia’s 50-acre search, then check which tracts can fit the building, yard and utilities.

guides.label: Prepare land for sale to a data center developer
guides.detail: Check the parcel, buildable acres and power evidence, then prepare a site submission or a buyer’s diligence file.

guides.label: Compare marketed land and asking terms
guides.detail: Find data center tracts and distinguish listing prices, offered boundaries, and the records behind power claims.

guides.label: Verify property tax and purchase exemptions
guides.detail: Compare a signed Fort Worth abatement with the Texas eligibility and certificate requirements for purchases.

guides.label: Find powered space and check occupancy
guides.detail: Separate leased or offered space from energized service and the capacity an occupant can use.

guides.label: Compare data center development projects for sale
guides.detail: Review marketed capacity, completed deal prices, site control, and the utility work each buyer still had to complete.

guides.label: Replay a parcel split or boundary change
guides.detail: Use dated tax maps and stable identity to recover the parcel geometry as of an earlier date.

guides.label: Screen collateral for commercial lending
guides.detail: Match ownership, permits, valuation, and hazards to the asset pledged for a loan.

guides.label: Find commercial property tax assessment history
guides.detail: Match a tax lot to its final assessments and reconcile taxable value to posted charges.

guides.label: Verify a commercial property tax abatement
guides.detail: Match the signed agreement to the equipment or parcel accounts and calculate the effect by taxing unit.

guides.label: Trace commercial mortgage maturity
guides.detail: Use dated loan and securitization records to distinguish scheduled maturity, extension options, and refinance exposure.

guides.label: Trace recorded commercial mortgage documents
guides.detail: Use 25 Water Street to link agreements and rent assignments without double-counting the indexed amount.

guides.label: Check a partial mortgage release by address
guides.detail: Compare two Manhattan records to distinguish the mortgage reference, the tax lot and the recorded release.

guides.label: Check property tax balances and lien status
guides.detail: Match the tax lot, compare the dated charge balance with notice history, and document the payoff or release evidence.

guides.label: Check property records for underwriting
guides.detail: Find building characteristics and exposure evidence for the property and effective date under review.

guides.label: Check replacement cost by building address
guides.detail: Compare seven modeled occupancy records with one tax lot and trace the 29% gap between the floor area sources.

guides.label: Check fire station distance and protection class
guides.detail: Compare mapped distance, a road route and the recognized response records behind a commercial property quote.

guides.label: Compare flood exposure at the asset boundary
guides.detail: Compare a Zone X address point with a building and tax lot that intersect Zone AE.

guides.label: Check wildfire hazard at the right building
guides.detail: Match two Los Angeles properties to their mapped buildings, then check which official hazard map covers each location.

guides.label: Check wildfire nonrenewal protections by ZIP code
guides.detail: Match an insured location to its emergency declaration, then check policy dates and the commercial property rules.

guides.label: Look up hail history for underwriting
guides.detail: Compare dated storm reports and radar cells near a property with the area’s long-run hail frequency.

guides.label: Use historical flood loss and claims data
guides.detail: Compare redacted NFIP records and keep privacy geography distinct from a property’s own loss history.

guides.label: Find potential grid headroom for a new load
guides.detail: Compare what public hosting maps and engineering evidence can tell you about a site.

guides.label: Compare Virginia and Ohio data center demand charges
guides.detail: See what a 100 MW July or November peak changes on Dominion’s December bill.

guides.label: Calculate minimum billed demand for a data center
guides.detail: Follow a 100 MW Ohio Power contract through the load ramp, the 11-month lookback and the primary base charges.

guides.label: Check what can run on conditional grid service
guides.detail: Use Southwest Power Pool’s tariff and a 100 MW example to estimate what remains online during a curtailment.

guides.label: Evaluate a power-flow study for a new facility
guides.detail: Read the modeled operating cases, limiting equipment, and conditions that affect the conclusion.

guides.label: Check a substation and its equipment
guides.detail: Distinguish the mapped facility, the rated equipment, and the evidence relevant to the proposed load.

guides.label: Trace the Texas large-load study process
guides.detail: Check the project’s application and evidence of utility review before relying on a service date.

guides.label: Compare ERCOT day-ahead and real-time prices
guides.detail: Download the historical hub series and align both hours of the fall clock change.

guides.label: Screen solar land and export capacity
guides.detail: Check usable land, the connection request, and the grid study assumptions behind the project.

guides.label: Track solar and battery interconnection requests
guides.detail: Follow the same queue IDs from a year-end snapshot to two operator reports and verify net export at the connection.

guides.label: Check grid import and export for a battery project
guides.detail: Compare when a battery may charge, when it may discharge, and which limits the proposed connection study covers.

guides.label: Check mapped water, sewer, and utility service
guides.detail: Find the serving provider and the evidence to request for a connection.

guides.label: Check water withdrawals, water rights, and allocation
guides.detail: Compare watershed data with permit conditions, treatment plans and confirmed utility service for a proposed site.

guides.label: Check natural gas capacity and service for a site
guides.detail: Compare posted pipeline capacity with firm transportation, fuel requirements and confirmed delivery at the meter.

guides.label: Verify fiber routes and entrance diversity
guides.detail: Compare the proposed paths and shared segments before calling two entrances independent.

guides.label: Check business broadband by address
guides.detail: Compare reported fiber, cable and fixed wireless, then get a provider quote for the exact building and suite.

guides.label: Find 100 buildable acres for manufacturing
guides.detail: Measure contiguous usable land and confirm rail, water, wastewater, and power for the tract on offer.

guides.label: Verify wastewater capacity for a factory
guides.detail: Check which sewer lines, pumps and plant allocations can serve the site, then confirm pretreatment and discharge limits.

guides.label: Compare industrial labor markets by county
guides.detail: Use worksite jobs, establishments, and industry concentration to decide which markets to investigate.

guides.label: Check truck routes and crossing restrictions
guides.detail: Replay two NYC route changes to check the corridor, vehicle limits and the dates behind each source.

guides.label: Check warehouse rail service and truck access
guides.detail: Use two Joliet listings to see what nearby tracks and advertised trailer counts establish.

guides.label: Reconstruct outage and road closure history
guides.detail: Check county electricity observations and actual reopening restrictions to evaluate site access and continuity.

guides.label: Track trade flows by commodity and mode
guides.detail: Compare entry, origin, and destination estimates and check separate border crossing counts.

guides.label: Find EV charging inventory and availability
guides.detail: Check port counts, live status, connector compatibility and the power a vehicle can draw when nearby ports are in use.

guides.label: Compare EV charger uptime and charge success
guides.detail: Recalculate California’s field results and see which records show annual uptime, live port status or a successful charge.

guides.label: Find electric truck charging along a freight route
guides.detail: Compare Long Beach, Colton and Blythe stops by fleet access, trailer fit, CCS or MCS connectors and usable power.

guides.label: Screen a fleet charging depot against its utility limit
guides.detail: Compare dispatch windows and charging schedules to see whether 5 MW can serve the proposed fleet.

guides.label: Compare drive-time demographics and a fixed radius
guides.detail: Use Detroit grocery sites to test how road access and Census sampling affect population, household income, and employment estimates.

guides.label: Compare a retail trade area before leasing
guides.detail: Distinguish reachable demand, nearby businesses, traffic, and actual store visits.

guides.label: Measure overlap between retail trade areas
guides.detail: Compare how many additional households a second store could reach across three drive-time cutoffs.

guides.label: Compare sidewalk foot traffic by block and time
guides.detail: Check comparable weekday and Saturday windows using published NYC pedestrian counts.

guides.label: Compare hourly heat and humidity
guides.detail: Reproduce a NOAA station benchmark for the cooling conditions a project will face.

guides.label: Trace water supply and discharge requirements
guides.detail: Check provider evidence, withdrawals, and permit steps for the planned cooling system.

guides.label: Link industrial permits to the right facility
guides.detail: Trace dated environmental records and verify the site identity before using them in diligence.

guides.label: Check environmental restrictions by address in NYC
guides.detail: Join the current tax lot to the zoning designation, cleanup record and recorded easement.

guides.label: Compare historical air quality and facility emissions
guides.detail: Reproduce EPA daily PM2.5 during the June 2023 smoke episode and compare it with the correct design value and facility inventory.

guides.label: Look up reported methane by facility
guides.detail: Use EPA facility IDs, direct emissions rows and reporting year to verify a gas plant’s methane total.

guides.label: Check oil and gas methane reporting and cost estimates
guides.detail: Find the EPA filing deadlines and trace which assumptions drive the proposed rule’s national compliance cost estimates.

guides.label: Compare Loudoun County data center counts by stage
guides.detail: Reconcile the county’s district counts with the map’s building points and look up the underlying permits.

guides.label: Track a development from hearing to decision
guides.detail: Find early construction leads and follow what happens to each separate application.

guides.label: Check highway bid results and contract awards
guides.detail: Match the TxDOT letting decision to the mapped project before using the bid amount or construction stage.

guides.label: Find government contract awards by work location
guides.detail: Track funding changes and connect a verified project location to parcel and transportation data.

title: U.S. site selection due diligence checklist
heading: Site selection due diligence
description: Use the tract, project requirements and dated evidence to decide whether a site belongs on your shortlist. Find field-tested guides for industrial, retail and energy projects.
imageAlt: Brooklyn Army Terminal from above, showing the clipped tax lot, mapped FEMA Zone AE and the published parcel coordinate.
imageCaption: Brooklyn Army Terminal. Parcel and flood overlay from the GIS API test below. Aerial imagery from NYS ITS, spring 2024.
checklistTitle: What to verify before making the shortlist

checks.title: The tract and the use
checks.detail: Get the current offering boundary and parcel IDs. Sketch the building, yard and access inside the usable area. Check permitted use, flood, wetlands and other land constraints against that layout.

checks.title: The service the project needs
checks.detail: Write down the required MW, water, wastewater and access by phase and date. Use local records to find who serves the tract, then ask each provider what can be delivered and which work it depends on.

checks.title: Evidence for each decision
checks.detail: Save the dated source and the tract or facility it describes. Give every open item an owner and a deadline. Keep a broker estimate, a screening result and a signed commitment distinct in the shortlist.

worksheet.label: Download the site evidence worksheet
worksheet.detail: Use one row for each requirement, tract and delivery phase.

guides.label: Evaluate a data center development acquisition
guides.detail: Trace what changes hands at closing, which power milestones remain, and who pays for utility construction.

guides.label: Screen a former power plant for redevelopment
guides.detail: Follow the Homer City records for generation, waste permit boundaries and county review, then check which evidence applies to your proposed layout.

guides.label: Compare a powered shell with a fitted data center
guides.detail: Identify the MW at the handoff, who pays for fit-out, and what starts the rent clock.

guides.label: Compare hourly heat and humidity for cooling
guides.detail: Replay the Phoenix and Dulles comparison from NOAA station records, and keep missing hours and climate normals visible.

guides.label: Screen land for wetlands and hydric soils
guides.detail: Compare mapped wetlands, soil map units and a Corps decision on a real property before drawing the development footprint.

guides.label: Review geologic maps, well logs, and site borings
guides.detail: Follow one industrial tax lot from its regional map to the nearby well reports and five on-site borings.

guides.label: Calculate slope and check usable acreage from lidar
guides.detail: Compare grid resolutions on the same land boundary and check the largest adjoining area that meets the slope cutoff.

guides.label: Check crop rotation, soil productivity, and irrigation
guides.detail: Compare annual crop maps against real plot records and confirm which source can support a farmland decision.

guides.label: Reconstruct outage and road closure history
guides.detail: Check county electricity observations and actual reopening restrictions to evaluate site access and continuity.

guides.label: Compare freight by geography, mode and commodity
guides.detail: Reproduce U.S. freight estimates for Canadian imports through Michigan and use BTS crossing counts as a separate check.

guides.label: Check hospital, school, and fire service coverage
guides.detail: Compare travel times, grade-specific attendance maps, and emergency service boundaries for a proposed housing development.

guides.label: Compare housing vacancy and rent burden by census tract
guides.detail: Match tract boundaries across Census releases and test whether changes in vacancy and rent burden exceed sampling uncertainty.

guides.label: Find infrastructure awards by where the work happens
guides.detail: Reconcile federal funding changes and verify the work location before screening parcel and access records.

guides.label: Track construction opportunities before permits are issued
guides.detail: Follow four Loudoun developments from agendas to decisions and see which applications actually moved forward.

guides.label: Compare GIS APIs for parcel, hazard and infrastructure screening
guides.detail: At Brooklyn Army Terminal, test what changes when you use the parcel boundary instead of the published coordinate.

guides.label: Find industrial land for sale by acreage and zoning
guides.detail: Replay Virginia’s 50-acre search, then check which tracts can fit the building, yard and utilities.

guides.label: Verify a shovel-ready site
guides.detail: Compare certified Tennessee sites against the same acreage and water requirements.

guides.label: Find 100 buildable acres for a manufacturing plant
guides.detail: Use the Camp Hall records to distinguish acreage on offer from the area that can fit a plant and yard.

guides.label: Verify the site’s tax incentives
guides.detail: Trace the city and county abatements for two Samsung equipment accounts and check the latest milestones.

guides.label: Confirm sewer capacity and pretreatment
guides.detail: Use the Camp Hall records to trace a proposed connection from the park to the receiving plant.

guides.label: Compare manufacturing clusters by county
guides.detail: Use BLS jobs, establishment counts and industry concentration to compare three Detroit-area counties.

guides.label: Check a warehouse’s rail access, truck route and trailer yard
guides.detail: Use two Joliet listings to test whether nearby tracks serve the building and how trailer counts vary by lease.

guides.label: Verify zoning across the whole site
guides.detail: Compare a point lookup, a tax lot record and five mapped districts at one Staten Island address.

guides.label: Trace environmental permits and enforcement
guides.detail: See why two EPA records linked to a Brooklyn facility fall outside the mapped tax lot.

guides.label: Compare historical air quality and facility emissions
guides.detail: Reproduce EPA daily PM2.5 during the June 2023 smoke episode and compare it with the correct design value and facility inventory.

guides.label: Screen a fleet depot for electric truck charging
guides.detail: Compare charging schedules and meter demand for a depot with a 5 MW service limit.

guides.label: Find electric truck charging near Long Beach and along I-10
guides.detail: Compare operating sites, limited fleet access and planned depots, with source dates and a dispatch calculation.

guides.label: Verify water and sewer service for a site
guides.detail: Compare the EPA map, county water and sewer classifications, and recorded volumes at a real Maryland project.

guides.label: Check water withdrawals, water rights, and allocation
guides.detail: Compare watershed data with permit conditions, treatment plans and confirmed utility service for a proposed site.

guides.label: Check natural gas capacity and service for a site
guides.detail: Compare posted pipeline capacity with firm transportation, fuel requirements and confirmed delivery at the meter.

guides.label: Compare grid capacity APIs for a new load
guides.detail: Use one National Grid feeder to distinguish seasonal load headroom from solar export capacity.

guides.label: Screen a solar site for land and export capacity
guides.detail: Trace a 200 MW Ohio uprate across two dated grid studies and compare the estimated upgrade costs.

guides.label: Track solar and battery interconnection requests
guides.detail: Follow the same queue IDs from a year-end snapshot to two operator reports and verify net export at the connection.

guides.label: Verify that a battery site can recharge on schedule
guides.detail: Compare import and export conditions and run an overnight recharge calculation.

guides.label: Calculate buildable acreage for a 100 MW IT campus
guides.detail: Replay a land budget with overlapping exclusions and two utility pad sizes, then compare the same area to the connected buildable polygons.

guides.label: Screen a data center site for phased power and permitting
guides.detail: Use the 12-check data center worksheet to evaluate power, land, water, fiber and approvals together.

guides.label: Compare day-ahead and real-time ERCOT prices
guides.detail: Reproduce the Houston and West hub comparison and keep both clock-change hours in the wholesale price analysis.

guides.label: Compare drive-time demographics and a fixed radius
guides.detail: Use Detroit grocery sites to test how road access and Census sampling affect population, household income, and employment estimates.

guides.label: Compare retail trade areas and foot traffic
guides.detail: Use the Harlem example to keep travel time, transit entries and actual store visits distinct.

title: Commercial property underwriting guides
heading: Commercial property underwriting
description: Build the property file before you quote. Match the building, verify flood, wildfire and hail evidence, and test the data behind the submission.
imageAlt: Illustration of a commercial building at the edge of dry Southern California hills
checklistTitle: What belongs in the property file?

checks.title: The building on the submission
checks.detail: Match the address, footprint and building ID to the statement of values, the schedule of insured locations and amounts. Review shared addresses and older footprints before applying a hazard result.

checks.title: Evidence dated to the decision
checks.detail: Keep the publisher, vintage and original result for each hazard layer or event. Record what was in effect on the quote or renewal date and when you retrieved it.

checks.title: The evidence still needed
checks.detail: Keep uncertain matches and coverage gaps visible. Request a dated inspection, roof scope or loss history when the available records leave a building-level question open.

worksheet.label: Download the underwriting API trial scorecard
worksheet.detail: Seven checks across four public cases. Record each provider’s building match, dates, sources and review outcome.

guides.label: Compare county-level NFIP flood payments
guides.detail: Use the current OpenFEMA endpoint to reproduce Hurricane Ida claim counts and net payments for two counties.

guides.label: Match a property address to the correct building outline
guides.detail: Test a campus address, three footprint polygons and a shared New York City tax lot.

guides.label: Compare flood risk APIs and test Zone X
guides.detail: Rebuild the parcel and building overlays at one Brooklyn store, then check what four Hurricane Ida marks show about mapped Zone X.

guides.label: Find an elevation certificate for the insured building
guides.detail: Compare the surveyed floor, floodproofing certification and a current county map lookup for a non-residential building.

guides.label: Compare underwriting data APIs
guides.detail: Compare ten providers and score the evidence behind each prefilled building, roof and hazard field.

guides.label: Verify a commercial replacement cost estimate
guides.detail: Match the building, compare modeled and recorded floor area, and keep reconstruction costs separate from tax values.

guides.label: Verify fire station and hydrant evidence
guides.detail: Use the Seattle routing case to check the responding station, water supply, and the rating method for an address.

guides.label: Check sprinkler permits and closeout by address
guides.detail: Join three New York City permits to their job records and see which floors each record covers.

guides.label: Verify building permit scope and completion
guides.detail: Use Brooklyn Army Terminal to distinguish permits from projects and roof replacement from rooftop equipment work.

guides.label: Check open building violations and correction records
guides.detail: Use the original building ID to verify summons status, balance and proof of correction on separate records.

guides.label: Check environmental restrictions before underwriting work
guides.detail: Compare the dated city requirements with the recorded state easement and site management plan.

guides.label: Verify when a commercial roof was replaced
guides.detail: Use Rosemead’s public records to test an address match, roof dates and provider evidence.

guides.label: Find the FEMA map in effect on the quote date
guides.detail: Use a real map revision to check the panel, decision date and buildings it covers.

guides.label: Check wildfire hazard for the right building
guides.detail: Replay two Los Angeles address and footprint checks against the 2025 CAL FIRE layer.

guides.label: Check California wildfire renewal protections
guides.detail: Compare the Dove and Gann Fire ZIP-code bulletins and review policy and notice dates under SB 547.

guides.label: Check hail history by address
guides.detail: Replay two Denver points across FEMA tract frequency, NOAA radar, storm reports and hail history APIs.

guides.label: Check hurricane wind history by address
guides.detail: Replay three Milton station checks and compare measured gusts with NOAA’s sustained-wind bands.

guides.label: Compare Florida hurricane claims by county
guides.detail: Use the Helene and Milton reporting dates to check county claim status and statewide commercial property losses.

guides.label: Check earthquake hazard by address
guides.detail: Compare two San Francisco address points using USGS seismic design cases and the city’s liquefaction layer.

title: Commercial real estate lending guides
heading: Commercial real estate lending
description: Build a dated credit file for a commercial real estate loan. Verify maturity dates, trace parcels and recorded instruments, and review flood and environmental evidence.
imageAlt: Aerial view of Midtown Manhattan with the Empire State Building tax parcel outlined
checklistTitle: What should the collateral file show?

checks.title: Which land and buildings secure the loan
checks.detail: Match the legal description and parcel identifiers to the actual collateral. Retain each prior identifier and its effective dates when the lot was split, merged or renumbered.

checks.title: Which documents supported the review
checks.detail: Save the deed, mortgage, assignment or release with its instrument number, dates and property references. Flag gaps and confirm the current title position through the title process.

checks.title: Which exposure questions are open
checks.detail: Match flood evidence to the relevant buildings and date. Check environmental facility and permit identifiers as well as the parcel. Record the documents still needed before closing.

guides.label: Match a property address to the correct building outline
guides.detail: Test a campus address, three footprint polygons and a shared New York City tax lot.

guides.label: Compare commercial property sales and lease terms
guides.detail: At one Manhattan tower, separate a deed from a lease assignment and compare recorded annual rent with a signed fixed-rent schedule.

guides.label: Check commercial space availability and lease rollover
guides.detail: Read dated leasing and occupancy metrics, verify available suites, and rebuild a public lease-expiration schedule.

guides.label: Get deed and ownership change alerts by address
guides.detail: Follow two NYC deeds through recording dates, instrument types and tax lot matches.

guides.label: Trace deeds, ownership and control
guides.detail: Follow two same-day deeds and a later change in decision rights at New York’s GM Building.

guides.label: Verify a commercial mortgage maturity date
guides.detail: Check which maturity belongs in a watchlist when quarter-end disclosures, signed changes, and conditional extensions give different dates.

guides.label: Look up commercial property income and debt-service coverage
guides.detail: Compare the two reported ratios, identify which properties they cover, and track the operating statement date through monthly filings.

guides.label: Check if a CMBS loan went into special servicing
guides.detail: Trace the EpiCentre loan through REO and liquidation using two monthly filings, then replay a watchlist with the published dates.

guides.label: Trace recorded commercial mortgage documents
guides.detail: Use 25 Water Street to link agreements and rent assignments without double-counting the indexed amount.

guides.label: Check a partial mortgage release by address
guides.detail: Follow the recorded reference back to the mortgage and check whether the lot identifiers match.

guides.label: Trace fixture filings and UCC-3 terminations
guides.detail: Check which financing statement each indexed termination references, even when the records share an address and recording date.

guides.label: Check property tax balances and lien status
guides.detail: Match the tax lot, compare the dated charge balance with notice history, and document the payoff or release evidence.

guides.label: Verify building permit scope and completion
guides.detail: Use Brooklyn Army Terminal to distinguish permits from projects and roof replacement from rooftop equipment work.

guides.label: Check open building violations before closing
guides.detail: Use the original building ID to verify summons status, balance and proof of correction on separate records.

guides.label: Compare property data APIs for credit review
guides.detail: Use three recorded instruments from the Empire State Building to test a collateral file as of a decision date.

guides.label: Verify property taxes for a credit file
guides.detail: Follow five years of Empire State Building assessments and reconcile two years of posted tax charges.

guides.label: Verify which tax benefits belong in the credit file
guides.detail: Check a signed city abatement and county actuals separately, then verify the facility’s purchase exemptions.

guides.label: Trace a parcel through a split or merger
guides.detail: Replay two New York City tax map changes and inspect how the prior IDs connect to the successor parcels.

guides.label: Verify the effective flood map for the collateral
guides.detail: Check the map date and any revisions that apply to the buildings securing the loan.

guides.label: Connect industrial land to permit and enforcement records
guides.detail: Use a Brooklyn facility to see where an address-only search can miss a regulatory record.

guides.label: Find environmental easements and restrictions on collateral
guides.detail: Trace a Brooklyn parcel through the city zoning index, state cleanup register and City Register.

guides.label: Review the power behind data center collateral
guides.detail: Identify the utility documents, capacity by phase and delivery conditions that support a powered-site assumption.

title: How to Evaluate Physical-World Data APIs
heading: Evaluating physical-world data APIs
description: Run eight real tests against physical-world data APIs. Compare parcel identity, zoning, flood exposure, property changes, underwriting records, power dates and charging.
imageAlt: Aerial view of Midtown Manhattan with the Digital Tax Map base lot for 432 Park Avenue outlined in gold.
imageCaption: 432 Park Avenue. The outline shows the Digital Tax Map base lot. Aerial imagery from NYS ITS, 2024.
checklistTitle: How to run a vendor trial

checks.title: Freeze the inputs and date
checks.detail: Write down the decision, exact location or ID, geometry, requested fields and date. Give every provider the same inputs. Alongside known answers, include a record that moved, split or should come back unknown.

checks.title: Set acceptance criteria before the demo
checks.detail: Use the worksheet’s dated reference result. Confirm the endpoint and what its fields measure. Record the returned entity, geometry, units, source and effective date. Keep an unavailable field separate from a failed request.

checks.title: Run it at production volume
checks.detail: Repeat the test across your actual counties and workload. Measure response times, failed requests and cost per usable result. Check retention, redistribution and audit rights for the data you will store or show, then document the gap owner and release decision.

worksheet.label: Download the vendor evaluation worksheet
worksheet.detail: Eight exact test inputs with dated reference results, original source links and space to record your vendor’s response.

guides.detail: Compare BBL 3039470001 before and after the November 20, 2026 split. The retained lot kept its ID and lost roughly 21,169 square feet.
